subject: English
passage: All advanced ceramics contain varying amounts of metallic oxides, stabilizing additives, and heat-resistant compounds. However, alumina-based ceramic, often used for industrial insulators, contains a higher percentage of aluminum oxide (at least 85%) than does zirconia-based ceramic and a higher concentration of silicon compounds, which is responsible for its thermal insulation properties. Unlike alumina-based ceramic, zirconia-based ceramic has a tetragonal crystalline structure resulting from the addition of yttria to the material. Zirconia-based ceramic has two subtypes: Type I grade, often used for dental crowns, and Type II grade, which has more yttria than Type I grade and is often used for cutting tools or abrasive components. Thus, ceramic material used to manufacture ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: industrial insulators will have a tetragonal crystalline structure.
choices.B: abrasive components will have similar thermal insulation properties to ceramic material used to manufacture industrial insulators.
choices.C: cutting tools will have a concentration of aluminum oxide lower than 85%, while ceramic material used to manufacture dental crowns will not.
choices.D: dental crowns will have a lower percentage of aluminum oxide in its composition than ceramic material used for industrial insulators will.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most logically synthesizes the passage's classification system. The text establishes that alumina-based ceramic, used for industrial insulators, contains at least 85% aluminum oxide. Zirconia-based ceramic is explicitly contrasted with alumina-based ceramic (note the transition "Unlike alumina-based ceramic, zirconia-based ceramic..."), indicating it has different compositional properties. Since dental crowns are made from Type I zirconia-based ceramic, they would contain a lower percentage of aluminum oxide than industrial insulators made from alumina-based ceramic with at least 85% aluminum oxide.
